PullRequest.Title: Fix Copilot CLI plugin updates on Windows
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- use the Copilot runtime's persisted `installedPlugins` records in `~/.copilot/config.json` as the authoritative installed-plugin inventory
- observe only the state file through a correlated non-recursive watcher; never watch the CLI cache recursively or open handles inside plugin directories
- validate committed `cache_path` records stay under the runtime-owned install root, preserve the last good inventory when state is malformed, and suppress unchanged state
- ignore redundant `chat.pluginLocations` entries into the CLI-owned cache and apply managed enablement to the authoritative discovery result instead of rediscovering cache folders
- leave live/local development plugins to configured, extension, and VS Code marketplace discovery, which retain in-place component watching
- remove VS Code's direct-delete action for CLI-owned plugins because CLI install/update/uninstall are lock-coordinated state transactions
- rebind MCP collections when a committed update rebuilds a plugin object at the same URI

Fixes #334391

Addresses the watcher trigger in #336864.

## Cross-client contract

This follows the same ownership model used by Copilot CLI and GitHub Copilot App:

- Copilot runtime persists a typed `installedPlugins` global-state array, writes it atomically under a per-file lock, and holds a cross-process plugin mutation lease across cache promotion/removal and dependent state writes.
- Cache replacement rolls back if the state transaction fails.
- Real installs persist `cache_path`; legacy records are accepted from the original snake-case `installed_plugins` key and resolve through both historical cache layouts when `cache_path` is absent.
- Live directory/local marketplace plugins are a separate non-persisted tier and are resolved per session.
- GitHub Copilot App asks runtime `plugins.list`, consumes stable plugin identities, and reacts to explicit `plugins_changed` invalidation; it does not enumerate cache directories.

## Automated validation

- 238 related plugin discovery, format, enablement, settings, installed-store, marketplace, install-service, and MCP discovery tests passed
- focused transaction tests cover committed versus uncommitted cache trees, config-only update signals, unchanged-state suppression, malformed-state retention, ancestor bootstrap/recreation, path confinement, and legacy fallback
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint for all changed implementation and test files
- Windows x64 assertion-backed UI scenarios using VS Code Dev 1.139.0 and the official Copilot CLI
- WSL 2 Ubuntu source-workbench validation using the official Linux Copilot CLI

## Original Windows reproduction

The unmodified build fails during the exact command `copilot plugin update spark@copilot-plugins` with `Access is denied. (os error 5)` while VS Code is open.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bceebba2-9f91-45fe-ab4c-162d20b8a126

## Final-head verification matrix

All 24 recorded Windows final-head steps passed with no skips and no window reloads. The additional WSL lifecycle passed 4/4 assertions without reloading.

### Official Copilot CLI lifecycle — 7/7 passed

Starts before `.copilot/config.json` exists, then verifies official CLI install, config-backed discovery, update, post-update discovery, uninstall, and UI removal.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e719ebe-df54-43bb-9b98-284a837b7601

### WSL 2 source-workbench lifecycle — 4/4 passed

Launches the Code OSS source build connected to Ubuntu, proves the remote filesystem provider is active, discovers `spark` from the Linux `~/.copilot` state and cache path, runs the official CLI update successfully, then observes official CLI uninstall remove the plugin without a window reload.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57ec7608-f3cb-45c2-b298-5fe02adc57ab

### Committed transaction behavior — 6/6 passed

Verifies uncommitted valid cache trees stay invisible, committed promotion appears, committed atomic replacement refreshes, committed removal clears inventory, and recreated state/cache recover without reload.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f10174c-c14f-448e-b8a8-7ef088a3abb1

### Managed plugin overlap — 3/3 passed

Verifies a CLI plugin also enabled by managed `chat.plugins.enabledPlugins` is discovered once from authoritative state, updates successfully with exit code 0, and remains visible.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7879fe8-c695-4b32-9256-bc8d33c23f7f

### Non-CLI live discovery regressions — 8/8 passed

Verifies configured Copilot and Claude plugins, extension-contributed Open Plugins, and VS Code-installed Agent Plugin marketplace sources retain live in-place component refresh, install, uninstall, and configured-location removal behavior.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d14eb12-c4fa-4123-b565-a98f60495a6c

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The state-change call path, unconditional eviction, and eager filesystem readers are directly traced in the changed code. Exact wall-clock impact depends on plugin count, component size, and local versus remote filesystem latency, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem resolve/read operations and rebuilt observable/plugin objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For each committed install, update, or uninstall, the cost grows with every installed CLI plugin and each plugin's component directories/files, even when only one installedPlugins record changed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive filesystem I/O and delayed plugin/MCP refresh after CLI transactions, especially on remote filesystems
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A discovery refresh reused an existing same-format plugin entry by URI, so unchanged plugins kept their parsed manifests and component observables; only relevant in-plugin watcher events refreshed changed contents.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Because every CLI source sets watchPluginContents to false, this condition disposes the existing entry for every source on every changed inventory refresh. The rebuild path then re-detects format, rereads the manifest, and eagerly starts reads for commands, skills, agents, rules, automations, hooks, and MCP definitions for all installed plugins.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `!watchPluginContents ||` branch at line 332 changes same-format URI entries from reusable to unconditionally disposable whenever content watching is disabled; this PR disables content watching for every CLI plugin source.
Findings.Title: Reuse unchanged CLI plugin entries across state refreshes
Findings.Impact: Updating or installing one plugin now causes collection-wide cache-directory I/O and object churn. With multiple plugins, particularly under vscode-remote, refresh fans out across all plugin component trees rather than the single changed record, increasing refresh latency and remote filesystem traffic.
Findings.Evidence: CopilotCliInstalledPluginsStore computes and compares a per-record revision, but _discoverPluginSources drops that revision and marks all sources watchPluginContents:false at line 1086. On any inventory difference, _refreshPlugins iterates all sources; this changed line evicts each existing no-watch entry. _toPlugin then calls readPluginManifest and creates seven recomputeInitiallyAndOnChange component readers whose parser helpers resolve directories and read files. The MCP identity check also re-registers collections for rebuilt objects, although stable server IDs avoid proving a subprocess restart.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep content watchers disabled, but propagate the store's revision or another stable content token into the plugin-entry cache and dispose/rebuild only entries whose revision changed; continue removing absent URIs through the existing seen-set cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup with Copilot CLI plugins installed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Agent-plugin and plugin-backed MCP availability waits for the initial inventory read and discovery/build; watcher attachment itself is not required for the first published inventory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe ancestors and create one non-recursive correlated watcher for ~/.copilot/config.json
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one directory resolve and one watcher; bounded by user-home path depth when .copilot does not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old implementation probed the installed-plugins ancestor chain and attached multiple directory/bucket watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Ancestor probing precedes watcher readiness but does not gate the initial direct getInstalledPlugins call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exist/read/parse config.json, resolve each cache path, detect format, read manifests, and enumerate component locations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One state-file exists/read, then P plugin-root resolves and P plugin builds; each build reaches manifest and component filesystem helpers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Startup scanned the installed root and B marketplace buckets, then performed format/manifest/component reads for each discovered plugin. The new state-file read replaces tree enumeration and removes per-plugin watchers, so no startup regression was established.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This work gates initial publication of CLI plugins and their MCP definitions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P committed CLI plugin records; for cache_path records effective cardinality is P plugin-root resolves plus per-plugin format, manifest, and component reads. Legacy records add up to two existence probes each.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Ancestor existence probes and the top-level plugin-source loop are sequential. Component observables start asynchronous directory/file reads as entries are built, so component I/O may overlap across plugins without a shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold startup performs the state and plugin reads; warm operation is event-driven and unchanged state is suppressed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: filesystem calls and initialization ordering are explicit in the implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin count, component size, and remote filesystem latency vary, but startup does not add collection-wide rebuilds beyond the cold build already required.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate startup finding: the new inventory read replaces broader directory enumeration and substantially reduces watcher count, while initial plugin content still must be built.

Scenarios.Scenario: Committed Copilot CLI install, update, or uninstall while VS Code remains open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the 200 ms state debounce, config parsing and the subsequent discovery/build must finish before the plugin list and plugin-backed MCP definitions reflect the committed transaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the committed config state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per coalesced config event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old implementation reacted to cache-directory events and did not read config.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates deciding whether plugin discovery must refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve every installed plugin and rebuild format, manifest, and all component readers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: P root resolves and P full plugin rebuilds for one changed record; each rebuild performs multiple component directory/file operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A refresh scanned root/bucket directories and detected formats, but same-URI same-format entries were reused, so unchanged plugins retained parsed manifests/component observables and only the affected plugin's content watcher refreshed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All rebuilt reads must settle through observables before complete updated plugin/MCP data is available; on remote providers each filesystem operation may cross the remote extension-host boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P installed CLI records after deduplication; a transaction changing one record still rebuilds all P no-watch plugin entries. Component cost additionally scales with files/directories in each plugin.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Config events coalesce through one RunOnceScheduler. The source loop is sequential through root resolve, format detection, and initial manifest read, while eagerly initialized component readers can create an aggregate asynchronous filesystem burst across rebuilt plugins.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: State reads are coalesced and equality-suppressed, but a real one-record revision change defeats reuse for every CLI plugin because watchPluginContents=false unconditionally evicts existing entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed eviction condition and eager component readers directly prove the P-wide repeated work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CLI transactions are user-driven and plugin inventories are usually bounded; exact delay depends on P, plugin tree size, and provider latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium repeated-work/I/O regression; finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Unrelated or unchanged Copilot config.json write
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A 200 ms debounced config read/parse occurs off the normal editor interaction path; equality suppression prevents plugin discovery and MCP updates when installedPlugins is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per coalesced relevant watcher burst, independent of P for cache_path records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old cache-directory watcher did not observe config-only writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not block normal interaction and stops before plugin discovery when inventory equality succeeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Config byte size and event frequency; events are coalesced to at most one pending refresh per debounce window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One scheduler coalesces watcher events; refreshes are asynchronous and no explicit overlapping-read guard exists, but ordinary watcher bursts collapse before execution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm inventory comparison suppresses unchanged publications and all component rereads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added read; low expected user-visible magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual config write frequency and file size are not established, but debounce and equality checks bound downstream cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this added boundary is debounced, bounded to one state file, and avoids downstream fan-out on unchanged state.

Scenarios.Scenario: First CLI install when ~/.copilot/config.json or its parent is absent, including deletion/recreation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The initial empty plugin inventory is published independently; detecting the later install waits for an ancestor watcher event, watcher rebinding, state refresh, and normal plugin discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve ancestors until one exists, attach a non-recursive watcher, then read the newly created state file
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resolve per ancestor level and one active watcher; one state read per coalesced creation/deletion event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old implementation similarly walked ancestors for the install root and attached multiple watchers down the cache hierarchy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only gates live detection after the initial empty result, not application startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Filesystem path depth from the missing .copilot directory to the nearest existing ancestor, then P committed plugin records after creation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Ancestor probes are sequential. RunOnceSchedulers coalesce watcher setup and state refresh; setup versions discard stale asynchronous watcher setup results.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Negative state is cached as an empty inventory but invalidated by the ancestor watcher, avoiding polling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setup versioning, mutable watcher ownership, and event filters are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Path depth is small and bounded; provider watcher latency varies.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: watcher/resource cardinality is lower than before and setup work is bounded by path depth.

Scenarios.Scenario: MCP collections when a CLI plugin object is rebuilt at the same URI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PluginMcpDiscovery synchronously disposes and re-registers the in-process collection before MCP consumers observe the new plugin definitions.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: M enabled plugins with MCP definitions; because the CLI refresh currently rebuilds all plugin identities, one transaction can rebind up to M collections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Collection disposal/registration is synchronous in one autorun. No subprocess/network concurrency is introduced; actual MCP process restart occurs only when the changed launch definition compares unequal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Collections are keyed by URI, but the new identity check intentionally invalidates the collection when the plugin object changes. McpService matches existing server objects by stable collection/server IDs and preserves them unless the actual server definition changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for collection churn and high that no independent subprocess fan-out is proven.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The amount of in-process registry/observable churn depends on M. No evidence shows unchanged server subprocesses restart, because McpService transfers servers by stable IDs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the unnecessary M-wide rebinding is downstream of the reported all-plugin rebuild; stable IDs prevent proving additional subprocess cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Configured/local plugin discovery overlapping the CLI-owned cache
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configured discovery resolves enabled paths before publishing configured plugins; paths under the CLI install root are now filtered and left to authoritative CLI discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve configured plugin paths outside the CLI cache
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolve per effective configured URI outside the CLI root; redundant CLI paths now incur no plugin stat/build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All configured paths, including duplicates into the CLI cache, were resolved and built with their own watchers.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configured pluginLocations entries and workspace folders used for relative expansion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configured entries are processed sequentially as before; no new parallel boundary burst is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CLI-cache duplicates are delegated to the state-backed discovery; non-CLI configured plugins keep existing warm entry reuse and watcher invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High based on the path filter and unchanged configured source behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Overlap prevalence is unknown, but the mechanism removes duplicate work rather than adding it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this path reduces duplicate filesystem reads and watchers.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all seven changed files. One medium-confidence-impact but high-mechanism-confidence repeated-work regression was submitted: a one-record CLI inventory change rebuilds every installed CLI plugin and its filesystem-backed components. Startup, watcher bootstrap, unchanged config writes, configured-path filtering, cleanup ownership, and MCP lifecycle were also traced; no additional subprocess, network, database, or independent memory regression was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
